title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and common internal templates. It is the canonical reference for cross-functional teams and should be referenced during onboarding, audits, procurement events, and major changes.

Owners and contacts

- Document owner: people-ops (primary contact: Ava Martinez, ava@redwood.example.com)
- Security/RBAC reviewer: Noah Kim (security)
- Finance/legal approver: Sofia Lopez (finance-legal)
- Escalation path: people-ops -> security -> finance-legal -> CTO

1) Access and permissions

Purpose: define how employees, contractors, and vendors are granted, reviewed, and revoked access to company systems. Applies to hosted cloud consoles, internal apps, production datasets, and on-prem components.

Principles:
- Least privilege: grant the minimal set of permissions required.
- Role-based access control (RBAC): use defined roles and groups; avoid ad-hoc owner-level grants.
- Time-bound access: temporary access for contractors and short-term projects must include an expiry date.
- Auditability: all changes must be traceable in audit logs.

Process: requesting access
1. Submit access request through the Access Request form (Confluence template link: Templates > Access Request). Include justification, required roles, duration, and owner.
2. People-ops routes to resource owner and security for approval. SLA: responses within 3 business days for standard requests; 24 hours for high-priority production access.
3. Approved requests are implemented by the responsible system owner or platform team; all grants are logged.

Periodic review
- Quarterly role membership review for all privileged groups (owners: service owners & security).
- Annual full user entitlement review (owner: people-ops + security).

Deprovisioning
- Offboarding checklist triggers automated revocation for cloud accounts, SSO sessions, and hardware access (owner: people-ops/IT). Target completion within 24 hours of termination event.

SSO and authentication standards
- SSO provider: Okta (production). All employees and contractors must use SSO.
- MFA: Required for all users with access to production or sensitive data (hardware token or authenticator app).
- Privileged access: require context-aware MFA and session short TTLs (max 1 hour).

Emergency access
- Break-glass accounts are tightly controlled, require 2-person approval, and are audited after use. Post-incident review required within 3 business days.

2) Change management

Scope: infrastructure changes, runtime changes, control plane upgrades, schema migrations, and any change that may affect production availability or data integrity.

Change categories and approval matrix:
- Class 1 (routine, low risk): configuration changes that do not affect customer-facing services. Approval: service owner. Scheduled during business hours.
- Class 2 (standard, medium risk): deployments to non-prod or non-critical services, performance tuning. Approval: service owner + eng-platform reviewer. Requires pre-deploy smoke tests.
- Class 3 (major, high risk): schema migrations, production deploys for critical services, runtime or kernel upgrades. Approval: service owner + eng-platform + security + on-call SRE. Requires change window and rollback plan.

Change request workflow
1. Create a Change Request in the Change Log (use template). Include: description, risk assessment, owners, rollback plan, test plan, scheduled window, and monitoring runbook.
2. Reviewers must comment within 48 hours; urgent requests may request expedited review.
3. Approved changes are scheduled; observers (security, SRE, product) are notified.
4. Execute, monitor for 30 minutes after change for critical services (or until baseline metrics are confirmed).
5. Post-change report: within 24 hours, owner uploads a short summary to the Change Log.

Change windows and blackout periods
- Regular change windows: Tue/Thu 02:00-06:00 UTC for disruptive infra changes (exceptions require exec approval).
- Blackout periods: major launches, end-of-quarter billing windows, and hotfix periods — no non-critical changes permitted.

3) Data management

Classification levels:
- Public: information intended for public consumption.
- Internal: non-sensitive internal documents and metadata.
- Confidential: business-sensitive information (pricing, contracts pre-signature).
- Restricted: regulated or personal data (PII, customer data with residency controls).

Data handling rules
- All data stores must declare a data classification label in metadata.
- Restricted data requires encryption at rest (KMS) and in transit (TLS 1.2+), network segmentation, and access via least-privilege roles only.
- Backup retention: default 90 days for Internal/Confidential, 365 days for Restricted unless legal instructs otherwise.
- Data residency: enforce region constraints for customer-specific Restricted data (owner: eng-private-deployments + security).

Data lifecycle and retention
- Data retention schedules must be documented per dataset. Use the Data Retention Template.
- Data minimization: only collect and retain data necessary for the business purpose.
- Deletion requests: people-ops and legal coordinate to validate and execute data deletion for customers/employees.

Data access for analytics
- Analysts requesting access to production datasets must: 1) request scoped read-only access, 2) provide justification, 3) agree to data handling checklist. Access is time-limited and logged.

Incident response and data breaches
- Follow the Incident Response policy (see related page). Data breach involving Restricted data triggers legal and security notification flows within 72 hours.

4) Procurement and expenses

Purpose: standardize purchasing, approvals, and reimbursement to ensure compliance and budget control.

Procurement thresholds and approvals:
| Amount (USD) | Approval required | Approver role | Comments |
|--------------|-------------------|---------------|----------|
| < $1,000     | Expense report    | Manager       | Standard monthly expenses |
| $1,000-25,000 | Purchase order    | Finance (procurement) + Manager | Requires vendor evaluation form |
| > $25,000    | Contract & PO     | Finance + Legal + Director-level signoff | RFP recommended for strategic vendors |

Process for purchases
1. Determine budget owner and cost center.
2. For standard vendor/software purchases, complete the Procurement Request template and vendor evaluation checklist.
3. Finance validates budget and issues PO where required. For purchases > $25k, legal must review contract terms (data residency, IP, indemnity).
4. Receipt and invoice: vendor invoices must be sent to finance@redwood.example.com and matched to PO within 5 business days.

Expenses and travel reimbursement
- Employees should use the Expense Report template. Submit within 30 days of expenditure.
- Receipts are required for all items > $25.
- Meal per diem: follow the published per-diem grid by region (link to Finance page).
- Corporate card policy: cardholders must reconcile monthly; violations are reviewed by Finance.

5) Vendor management and onboarding

Objective: ensure vendors meet security, privacy, and contractual standards before access or payment.

Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Completed vendor intake form with scope of work and contacts.
- Security questionnaire completed and assessed (if vendor handles Restricted data, must complete full security questionnaire).
- Signed NDA and contract with clearly defined SLAs and termination clauses.
- Data handling addendum for vendors that process customer or employee personal data.
- Insurance certificate and SOC 2 / audit evidence where applicable.

Ongoing vendor governance
- Quarterly vendor performance and risk reviews for strategic vendors (owner: procurement + vendor owner).
- Access reviews: vendor accounts and privileges reviewed monthly while active.
- Exit plan: contract must include data return or secure destruction clauses.

Termination process
1. Notify vendor and internal stakeholders.
2. Revoke all access (SSO, keys, service accounts).
3. Validate data destruction or return.
4. Final invoice reconciliation and close-out report.

6) Travel policy

Purpose: a clear, fair travel policy that balances employee safety, cost control, and productivity.

Booking and approvals
- All business travel must be pre-approved via the Travel Request template with estimated budget. Manager approval required; trips > $5,000 also require Director approval.
- Use preferred travel vendors for corporate rates where available.

Allowed expenses
- Flights: economy class for trips < 6 hours; premium economy or business require Director approval.
- Lodging: mid-range hotels; exceptions for safety or logistics must be documented.
- Ground transport: rideshare or taxis; rental car allowed if pre-approved.

Safety and emergency
- Employees must register travel plans with people-ops for trips to regions flagged by Travel Advisory.
- In emergencies, contact people-ops (24/7 emergency line provided in corporate phonebook).

Reimbursement
- Submit expense reports within 30 days with itemized receipts. Delayed submissions may be declined.
- Cardholder vs. reimbursed expense rules are in the Expense Template.

7) Internal templates and repositories

Standard templates included on this page (link to Templates folder):
- Access Request template (required fields: resource, role, justification, expiry)
- Change Request template (description, risk, rollback plan, monitoring metrics)
- Procurement Request and Vendor Evaluation templates
- Expense Report & Travel Request templates
- Data Retention and Data Classification templates

Template usage guidance
- Always use the canonical templates in the Templates folder; do not create ad-hoc forms for approvals.
- When creating a custom instance, reference the owner_team and include an expiration if temporary.

Governance, exceptions, and review cadence
- Exceptions to any policy must be submitted using the Policy Exception template and approved by two approvers (people-ops + either security or finance-legal depending on the exception).
- Policy review schedule: major policies reviewed annually; operational procedures reviewed quarterly.
- Compliance evidence: owners must maintain evidence artifacts (audit logs, approval emails, PO records) for at least the retention period defined in the Data Retention policy.

Appendices

- People-ops: people-ops@redwood.example.com

B. Change risk matrix (short form)
- Low: config changes, documentation updates.
- Medium: non-prod deployments, performance tuning.
- High: schema migrations, production kernel/runtime updates.
